question: Does a particular full-attention head causally contribute to retrieval when the two words must be assembled from separately listed facts?
selection: Use the 9B phrase-development block screen, choosing between full-attention blocks 19 and 23 by largest donor-minus-random gain. Keep this block for both models; apply a second development screen separately per model for head identity. Swap one of 16 gated head outputs at the last position from the other clean query. Select the largest average alternate-answer margin increase, lowest head on ties. No outcomes from the four-person assembly test enter selection.
test: Seed 31033, 64 unique four-person records. Prefix lists first words and final words in two independently permuted sections. Two queried people share a first word but have distinct second words. Other two people share a different first word. The four suffixes differ; the queried pair is balanced by random fact order. The query changes a single name. Word banks are token-filtered on each checkpoint. No clean-failure exclusion.
heads: Positive control: substitute all 16 gated outputs together before the output projection. Primary: selected-head gain minus mean of offset +3,+7,+11 same-layer head gains, prefix-paired bootstrap. Also evaluate all except the selected head and identity substitution. Report joint effect and the marginal contribution when the other fifteen have already been swapped. Do not sum logit effects or infer unique mediation.
uncertainty: Two symmetric queries per record, 10000 bootstrap draws of whole records. Primary on 9B; 4B tests the same selection procedure and block without assuming homologous head number.
prior_component: Retest previously identified 9B block 23 head 0 on all four-person assembly test rows, regardless of newly selected layer or head. Report its head-only gain and paired difference vs the newly selected head. Evaluate the same indexed site descriptively on 4B.
